story_type: Marine helicopters carry seawater buckets into a base wildfire
hook: Marines dropped seawater from a bucket right onto the flames.
narration: This Marine helicopter dumped its bucket of water straight onto the flames.
In May 2014, wildfires broke out across Camp Pendleton, the huge Marine base on the California coast.
One of them, the Las Pulgas fire, grew to six hundred acres on its first afternoon, with zero containment.
Two whole camps on the base were ordered to evacuate.
So the Marines of Helicopter Squadron 364 took off to help Cal Fire.
They filled their buckets straight from the Pacific Ocean.
The bucket hangs on a long line, scoops up water, and opens a valve in its bottom to drop it right on the fire.
From the open door, the crew chief watched the fire line slide past below.
[short pause] The flames ran in long lines through the brush, under a sky turned orange by smoke.
Then they flew back for more water, again and again.
outcome: The biggest fire reached seventy-five percent containment, and Camp Pendleton went back to normal operations.
title: Marines haul seawater into a wildfire
description:
In May 2014, Marine Medium Helicopter Squadron 364 helped Cal Fire and local agencies fight the wildfires burning across Marine Corps Base Camp Pendleton, California, scooping water from the Pacific and dropping it on the fire lines.
